Section D

Executive summary by product

Entra

  • Entra Connect Sync mandatory upgrade — all sync services stop entirely on 2026-09-30 for any server below v2.5.79.0 — verify tenant-wide version now, this is a hard cutoff not a soft degradation. [source]
  • Federated Token Validation Policy enforcement — Entra now blocks federated sign-in by default on UPN-domain mismatch (updated 2026-08-18) — review federation config or expect AADSTS5000820 failures. [source]
  • memberOf dynamic-group operator retiring 2026-11-03 — groups freeze silently, no error — audit privileged/role-assignable dynamic groups using memberOf now. [source]
  • Passkeys become the tenant-wide default 2026-09-01 — SMS/Voice-enabled users are auto-enrolled into passkey registration — size exposure with the SMS/Voice usage analyzer before rollout. [source]
  • Black Hat passkey-replay research disclosed — a now-patched Windows event-log flaw allowed passkey assertion replay (up to Global Admin impersonation); unpatched attack classes remain — reinforce PAWs and EDR coverage for admins. [source]

Microsoft Sentinel

  • SAP containerized connector retires 2026-09-14 — analytics rules/workbooks/hunts on SAP logs silently stop returning results — migrate to the GA agentless SAP connector now. [source]
  • 10 new UEBA anomaly rules — Check Point/FortiGate/Zscaler/AWS GuardDuty now feed UEBA anomaly detection — enable UEBA on the relevant connectors to benefit. [source]
  • SAP BTP analytic rules renamed — existing rules gained an 'SAP BTP' prefix — check saved references, automation rules, and dashboards that pointed to the old names. [source]

Defender family (XDR / MDE / MDI / Cloud Apps)

  • Defender for Cloud Apps: Unified RBAC default for new tenants — verify analyst role assignments reflect Unified RBAC rather than legacy MCAS-native roles on any new onboarding. [source]
  • MDI: expanded automatic auditing for AD CS/AD FS/Entra Connect servers — sensor v3.x now auto-configures required auditing on these role servers — verify sensor coverage to benefit. [source]
  • MDE: Linux AV audit mode + offboarding API GA — audit-mode hosts alert but don't quarantine — confirm dashboards flag audit-mode hosts clearly so alert-only isn't mistaken for blocked. [source]
  • Exposure Management: Codename MDASH gains Azure DevOps connector — agentic code-security scanning now extends beyond GitHub to ADO repos. [source]
  • AIAgentsInfo table already retired from queryability (2026-07-01, elapsed) — any saved/API-driven KQL still referencing AIAgentsInfo instead of AgentsInfo may already be broken — check now. [source]

Microsoft Graph

  • Legacy security alerts API (v1) retirement pushed to 2026-10-15 — still being retired — confirm SIEM/SOAR pipelines have migrated to alerts_v2/incidents. [source]
  • Entra directory object recovery API reaches GA — new IR/DR capability for tenant tampering or bulk-deletion — review who can call it and add to runbooks. [source]
  • distributionList.members (beta) breaking change — standalone list/get-members methods removed in favor of $expand=members — any beta integration reading DL membership the old way breaks now. [source]
  • Beta responseAction resource types removed 2026-10-01 — custom-detection automation must migrate to automatedAction/automatedActionSet before the cutover. [source]

Microsoft Intune

  • RBAC Scoped permissions moving to GA — becomes default for ALL tenants — run the Permissions Assessment Report now to preview effective-permission changes before it ships. [source]
  • ASR Device Control extends to MDE-attach (non-Intune-enrolled) devices — check current policy assignments now to confirm only intended devices receive it once this ships. [source]
  • Google Play Strong Integrity enforcement 2026-10-31 — unpatched Android 13+ devices lose Strong Integrity and can trip app-protection/compliance blocks — audit patch-level settings now. [source]
  • Policy Configuration Agent / Change Review Agent removed 2026-08-31 — finish any in-flight Security-Copilot-agent activity now; already-created policies are unaffected. [source]

Microsoft Purview

  • Auto-labeling policy simulation mode — run new/edited auto-labeling policies in simulation first to avoid mislabeling before enforcement. [source]
  • Auto-labeling policy Insights tab — new at-a-glance performance view for ongoing DLP/IP governance auditing. [source]

Section I

KQL and threat hunting

No advanced-hunting schema change was dated inside the strict 2026-08-13–2026-08-27 window (the AIAgentsInfo → AgentsInfo table migration is real and high-value, but Microsoft dates it to the June 2026 what's-new bucket, with its migration deadline of 2026-07-01 already elapsed — see Section H, Defender XDR). Per the brief's own fallback rule, three practical hunting queries and three detection-engineering ideas tied to this run's findings follow instead. Every table/column name below is verified against the cited Microsoft Learn schema page as of 2026-08-27; nothing is invented.

1. Hunt — federated sign-ins blocked by the new Federated Token Validation Policy

Change: Entra now blocks federated sign-in on UPN-domain mismatch by default (MC1303719, updated 2026-08-18). Operational benefit: surfaces the scope of impact before/while enforcement completes, and any user or app hitting the new default block. SOC use case: triage helpdesk tickets citing sign-in failures during the rollout window; confirm the block is intentional federation-trust protection, not an outage.

SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ResultType == "5000820"
| summarize Attempts = count(), AffectedUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName) by AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName
| order by Attempts desc

Schema verified against SigninLogs table reference (ResultType, AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName confirmed columns; UserPrincipalName confirmed via the table's own sample queries). The exact ResultType string for AADSTS5000820 is (inferred) — confirm against a real blocked sign-in in your own tenant before relying on it in an analytics rule.

2. Hunt — authentication failures on AD CS / AD FS / Entra Connect role servers

Change: MDI sensor v3.x now auto-configures auditing on these servers (Aug 2026). Operational benefit: the moment auditing lands, this query starts returning real signal on certificate-services/Entra-Connect-account abuse attempts that were previously invisible. SOC use case: baseline failed-logon patterns on these role servers now, before the expanded auditing changes what "normal" looks like.

IdentityLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("adfs", "adcs", "aadc", "connect")
| where isnotempty(FailureReason)
| summarize FailedLogons = count() by AccountUpn, DeviceName, Protocol, FailureReason
| order by FailedLogons desc

Schema verified against IdentityLogonEvents table reference (Timestamp, DeviceName, FailureReason, AccountUpn, Protocol all confirmed columns). The has_any server-name substrings are an example pattern — adjust to your actual AD CS/AD FS/Entra Connect host-naming convention.

3. Hunt — continued calls to the legacy Graph security alerts API (v1) ahead of its Oct 15 retirement

Change: the legacy /security/alerts endpoint's retirement date moved from Aug 31 to Oct 15, 2026 (Section G). Operational benefit: finds exactly which app registrations still call the endpoint being retired, so migration can be targeted rather than guessed at. SOC use case: feed the resulting AppId list into a tracked migration list; re-run weekly until it returns zero rows.

GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RequestUri has "/security/alerts" and RequestUri !has "alerts_v2"
| summarize Calls = count(), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by ApplicationId, ServicePrincipalId, RequestUri
| order by Calls desc

Schema verified against GraphAPIAuditEvents table reference (RequestUri, ApplicationId, ServicePrincipalId, Timestamp all confirmed columns).

Detection-engineering ideas

  1. Analytics rule on AADSTS5000820 spikes — alert when Hunt #1 crosses a per-app threshold in a rolling 1-hour window; a sudden spike right after the mid-August rollout more likely indicates a legitimate federation-trust misconfiguration than a security incident, but a slow trickle weeks later is worth investigating as a possible probing pattern.
  2. Dynamic-group membership staleness watch — for any privileged/role-assignable group, alert when a group configured with the memberOf operator shows zero AuditLogs "Add member to group"/"Remove member to group" events for >7 days while the tenant's overall joiner-mover-leaver activity continues — an early warning the group has silently frozen ahead of the Nov 3 memberOf retirement.
  3. SAP connector heartbeat — a scheduled analytics rule on the ingestion table backing the SAP containerized connector that fires if no new SAP-sourced event lands within an expected interval after 2026-09-14, catching a missed migration as a coverage gap rather than discovering it during an incident.

Section M

Strategic watchlist

3-12 month initiatives to track — no action this week, all require a plan.

  • SMS/Voice authentication full retirement (2027-02-01) — Passkeys become mandatory for any account still on Microsoft-provided SMS/Voice — plan the full migration path over the next two quarters, not just the Sept 1 default-rollout step. source ↗
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS) full retirement (2027-04-01) — Every EWS-dependent integration (SIEM connectors, legacy mailbox tools) needs a Graph API migration plan well before the phased disablement starting Oct 2026 becomes a full cutoff. source ↗
  • Microsoft Sentinel's move to the Defender portal only (2027-03-31) — Any team still standardized on the Azure-portal Sentinel experience should plan analyst workflow/tooling migration to the Defender portal over the coming year. source ↗
  • Defender for Cloud Apps file-policy deprecation in favor of Purview DLP (2027-01-06) — Policies do not auto-migrate — a multi-quarter recreation effort for any org with a sizeable file-policy estate. source ↗
  • Intune RBAC Scoped Permissions becoming the tenant-wide default — A structural change to how effective permissions are computed — worth a dedicated access-model review, not just a pre-GA report run. source ↗
  • Agentic-identity and AI-agent governance maturing across Entra/Defender/Intune — Agent ID Administrator, AI-agent posture risk scoring, prohibited-local-AI-agent compliance detection, and Copilot-agent identity models are all landing within months of each other — track as one converging governance program, not isolated features. source ↗
  • Full non-Graph API permission surface inventory (12 surfaces still queued) — Exchange Online, Azure Service Management, SharePoint, and nine others remain outside this catalog's coverage — track completion of the queue over the coming weeks as a data-quality milestone for this briefing itself. source ↗
  • Azure RBAC full role inventory (not yet started) — This catalog covers all 137 Entra directory roles but none of Azure RBAC's ~120 built-in roles yet — a natural next expansion for the Roles catalog. source ↗
